claims.claim: We also deals on all kinds of car spare parts
claims.evidence: The witness report only shows an engine assembly; it does not confirm the seller’s business scope or that this specific item is included in that claim.

risks.risk: Engine make/model is not identifiable from the photos, so compatibility and replacement cost are unknown.
risks.proof: A clear close-up of the engine identification plate/badge and/or stamped engine number (and brand/model markings) in the same frame.
risks.if_unproven: Price as an unidentified used engine assembly with unknown fitment and unknown parts availability.

risks.risk: Unknown running condition (no evidence of start, compression, leak-down, overheating, or smoke).
risks.proof: A short video of the engine starting and idling (or a compression/leak-down test sheet with matching engine number).
risks.if_unproven: Price as non-tested/untested engine assembly (worst case: may be defective).

risks.risk: Completeness is uncertain (photos don’t confirm whether it includes all required components like turbo, sensors, wiring harness sections, mounts, intake/exhaust manifolds, or transmission mating parts).
risks.proof: A full laid-out inventory photo/clip showing every included component, plus a checklist of what’s included (turbo, alternator, starter, ECU/sensors if applicable, mounts, hoses, wiring connectors).
risks.if_unproven: Price as potentially incomplete assembly; assume missing/extra-cost parts.

risks.risk: Suspension struts/spring units are visible, but it’s unclear whether they are included as part of the engine package or separate—this affects value and what you’re actually buying.
risks.proof: A clip showing the full set of items being sold together (engine + any struts/springs) with clear labeling of what is included.
risks.if_unproven: Price as engine assembly only, treating the visible strut/spring units as uncertain inclusion.

risks.risk: Potential major damage not visible in the provided angles (cracks, bent shafts, seized turbo, damaged turbo/exhaust housing, stripped connectors).
risks.proof: Close-ups of turbo/exhaust housing, intake/exhaust ports, crank pulley area, and all connector ends; plus a test showing no abnormal noise/boost issues.
risks.if_unproven: Price at worst-case for internal/external damage risk (as-is, no warranty).

risks.risk: Fluid condition and contamination (oil/coolant leaks, sludge, water ingress) can’t be confirmed from the photos.
risks.proof: Photos of oil fill/dipstick condition, coolant reservoir/radiator-side condition (if present), and any leak points; ideally a drain/inspection clip.
risks.if_unproven: Price as unknown fluid condition with possible contamination.

proof_requests: Send clear close-up photos of the engine make/model and stamped engine number/label (readable).
Provide a short video of the engine starting and idling (or compression/leak-down test results) with the engine number visible.
Confirm completeness: list exactly what is included (turbo, intake/exhaust manifolds, alternator, starter, sensors, wiring harness sections, mounts, and any transmission-related parts if present).
Show close-ups of the turbo/exhaust housing and all connector ends to rule out cracks/seizure/stripped parts.
Confirm whether the visible strut/spring units are included in the sale and show the full set of items together.
response.reason: The witness confirms it’s a used engine assembly with visible strut/spring units, but key pricing drivers (engine identity, running condition, completeness, and damage level) are not verifiable from the provided angles. Without at least engine identification and a running/test proof, a reliable worst-case price cannot be set confidently.
